title: Naming the Savings Account a Personal Checking Account Draws On
content:
Where a Personal Checking account has been paid into overdraft and its record names no protection source, the record owes one.

A Personal Checking account may name one of the owner's own savings accounts as the protection source the bank draws on to cover an item that would otherwise overdraw it, and because it is the owner's own savings that would be drawn on, the owner names it in person.

A savings account that is not the owner's own or is not in active status is never named, whatever cover it carries.

## Recording the source

The tool `authorize_overdraft_protection_source_1d4e232c` is unlocked and handed over for the customer themselves to run, since the savings account being committed is theirs. One run writes that savings account onto the checking account as its protection source, replacing whatever source was named there before. No money moves during the run, nothing is charged, and the owner then sees the savings account shown as the protection source on the checking account.

### Parameters

- `checking_account_id` — the reference number of the Personal Checking account that is to be protected, taken from the checking account lookup for this owner. Reference number.
- `overdraft_link_savings_account_id` — the reference number of the owner's savings or money market account that is to be drawn on, read from the savings account lookup. An empty string leaves the checking account with no protection source at all. Reference number.

### Return

The run answers with a confirmation sentence naming the checking account reference number and the savings account reference number now recorded as its protection source. That sentence naming the savings account is what shows the run completed; the checking account lookup then shows it as the protection source.
